● Task 2 is complete and verified. Now to your toolbar clipping report — I don't want it buried in the sidebar work, so let me address it
  directly.

  What you're describing: 1–2 characters clipped on the right edge of the toolbar, mostly when the labels are long enough to reach
  that edge. Given the architecture (custom flex layout + native scroll), my leading hypothesis is a width mismatch between the
  container and its children: the toolbar is sized to N buttons, but the rendered row's actual pixel width slightly exceeds the visible
  area, so the rightmost button gets clipped by overflow. The "long labels, not always" pattern fits — you only see it when content
  actually reaches the last slot. A common specific cause is a vertical scrollbar appearing and stealing width the layout did not
  account for (so it clips once it grows).

  That's a hypothesis, not a diagnosis — pinning it down properly means reproducing it with a screenshot, checking the width
  computation against the container measurement, and writing a failing test, which is its own focused debugging session.

  How do you want to sequence it?
